messages:
Samir (SE): Heads-up — onboarding call with EdgeBank POC tomorrow. They want to stream responses over gRPC with multiplexed sessions from our Rust SDK and enforce strict structured JSON output for downstream validators. Also flagged: backpressure on large customer transcripts, and a security questionnaire asking about retention/KMS. Any quick wins?

Maya (Solutions): Nice. Two quick things: 1) structured output — recommend function-calling or our structured output post-hook + schema check in client. 2) streaming + multiplexing — use connection-per-tenant vs full multiplex depending on auth isolation. Which one did they request?

Samir (SE): They asked for multiplexing (many user sessions over a single channel) to avoid TLS churn. They also want a simple assertion harness: each message must return valid JSON with keys: {\"intent\":string, \"entities\":[], \"confidence\":float}. If malformed — reject.

Leo (Runtime): Multiplexing is supported but caveats: KV cache / prefix caching currently scoped per logical session id. For many concurrent sessions you'll want to attach a session_id header so KV cache doesn't bleed prefixes. Also watch max_inflight per connection to avoid backpressure.

Samir (SE): Can you sketch config flags I should pass to the Rust SDK example?

Maya (Solutions): Sure — for Rust SDK streaming multiplexed pattern (pseudo):

```rust
let client = Redwood::new("API_KEY");
let stream = client.stream_with_headers(&endpoint)
    .header("x-tenant-id", tenant_id)
    .header("x-session-id", session_id)
    .max_inflight(8)
    .on_event(|chunk| parse_json_assert(&chunk));
```

Set `max_inflight=8` and `session_id` per logical chat to keep KV prefix isolation.

Leo (Runtime): Also set `prefix_kv_cache=true` on the server side for these tenants. That will give big token savings for repeated system prompts. If you see backpressure increase, reduce `max_batch_tokens` or enable burst capacity on Dedicated.

Priya (Product): For structured assertions, two recommended approaches: 1) function-calling with a strict schema -> model returns typed fields; 2) a lightweight post-processor that validates JSON and retries with a stricter prompt (e.g., "Return only JSON, no prose"). For evaluation we can wire that into Redwood Optimize to track regression metrics (schema fail rate, avg confidence).

Samir (SE): Good. EdgeBank also asked about pricing: if they stream 500 concurrent sessions with average 150 tokens/sec, what should we recommend — Hosted vs Dedicated?

Ben (AE): For sustained throughput at that scale Dedicated reserved is usually cheaper — we can run numbers but expect a 30–50% unit cost reduction vs bursty hosted. Also Dedicated gives you guaranteed latency SLOs for critical banking flows. I'll pull a cost sketch.

Samir (SE): Thanks. Security questionnaire Qs: "Do you retain request payloads? How long? Where encrypted?" What's the short answer we can give for the POC?

Priya (Product): Short/POC answer (suitable for presales): "Request logs are retained for 30 days by default for debug/analytics, encryption at rest using customer-managed keys is available for Private deployments (KMS/HSM integration). Hosted customers can request reduced retention or opt-out for sensitive flows — we also support token redaction and field-level hashing in transit." (we'll hand off full questionnaire to security for formal sign-off).

Samir (SE): Perfect. Any production pitfalls we should warn them about?

Leo (Runtime): A couple: 1) ensure session-level nonce in headers so prefix caching is safe; 2) monitor client-side event loop — if you buffer too much server-side, clients will see long tail latency; 3) function-calling deterministic setup: use temp=0 and top_p low if you need strict field values.

Samir (SE): Noted. I'll bring up these items on the call and ask if they want a short canary test with 50 simultaneous multiplexed sessions.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment launched: presales-multiplex-canary (50 sessions) — started 1788887805. Logs: http://internal/deploys/1788

Maya (Solutions): Awesome — tag me in the canary and I'll validate schema fail rate. If we see >2% schema failures we should enable post-process retry with a structured prompt.

Ben (AE): I'll attach an initial pricing sketch and the security Q stub to the follow-up email to EdgeBank. Samir, want me to join the call?

Samir (SE): Yes please — having you there to discuss Dedicated economics will help. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
